extracted.intended_audience: public water system operators, state drinking water regulators, and compliance officers responsible for Subpart H and Subpart T drinking water requirements
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory compliance requirements for ground water public water systems (Subpart H) and enhanced filtration/disinfection for systems serving fewer than 10,000 (Subpart T), including monitoring, corrective actions, public notification, reporting, recordkeeping, and turbidity/disinfection performance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of treatment technique requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The treatment technique requirements of this section must be met by ground water systems when a significant deficiency is identified or when a ground water source sample collected under § 141.402(a)(3) is fecal indicator-positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may direct applicability for samples collected under § 141.402(a)(2), § 141.402(a)(4), or § 141.402(b). When a significant deficiency is identified at a Subpart H system using both ground and surface water or GWUDI, system must comply except where State determines deficiency is in portion served solely by surface water or GWUDI.

rubrics_metrics.name: State consultation within 30 days after notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the State directs the ground water system to implement a specific corrective action, the ground water system must consult with the State regarding the appropriate corrective action within 30 days of receiving written notice from the State of a significant deficiency, written notice from a laboratory that a ground water source sample collected under § 141.402(a)(3) was fecal indicator-positive, or direction from the State that a fecal indicator-positive collected under § 141.402(a)(2), § 141.402(a)(4), or § 141.402(b) requires corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant deficiencies include, but are not limited to, defects in design, operation, or maintenance, or failure/malfunction of sources, treatment, storage, or distribution that the State determines are causing or have potential for causing contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: 120-day corrective action or state-approved plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days (or earlier if directed by the State) of receiving written notification of a significant deficiency or fecal indicator-positive sample, the ground water system must either (i) have completed corrective action in accordance with applicable State plan review processes or other State guidance, including State-specified interim measures; or (ii) be in compliance with a State-approved corrective action plan and schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent modifications to a State-approved corrective action plan must be approved by the State. If the State specifies interim measures pending plan approval or completion, the system must comply with interim measures and any State-specified schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground water systems that meet the conditions of paragraphs (a)(1) or (a)(2) must implement one or more of the following corrective action alternatives: (i) Correct all significant deficiencies; (ii) Provide an alternate source of water; (iii) Eliminate the source of contamination; or (iv) Provide treatment that reliably achieves at least 4-log treatment of viruses (using inactivation, removal, or a State-approved combination) before or at the first customer for the ground water source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems may implement one or multiple alternatives as appropriate and as approved/directed by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special public notice for significant deficiencies or fecal contamination
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the applicable public notification requirements of § 141.202, systems receiving notice from the State of a significant deficiency or fecal indicator-positive ground water source sample that is not invalidated must inform the public of the fecal indicator-positive source sample or of any significant deficiency that has not been corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community systems must inform public under § 141.153(h)(6) and continue annually until corrected; non-community systems must inform in a State-approved manner within 12 months of notification (or earlier if directed) and continue annually; required information includes nature and date of deficiency, State-approved plan/schedule including interim measures and progress, and language assistance provisions for large proportions of non-English speaking consumers. If directed, corrected non-community systems must inform customers how and when deficiencies were corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification for existing ground water sources providing 4-log treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A ground water system not required to meet source water monitoring because it provides at least 4-log treatment of viruses before or at the first customer before Dec 1, 2009 must notify the State in writing that it provides at least 4-log treatment and begin compliance monitoring by Dec 1, 2009.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must include engineering, operational, or other information the State requests. If the system subsequently discontinues 4-log treatment, it must conduct source water monitoring as required under § 141.402.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for new ground water sources providing 4-log treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A ground water system placing a ground water source in service after Nov 30, 2009 that is not required to meet source water monitoring because it provides at least 4-log treatment must: (i) notify the State in writing that it provides at least 4-log treatment (including requested information); (ii) conduct compliance monitoring under § 141.403(b)(3) within 30 days of placing the source in service; and (iii) conduct ground water source monitoring under § 141.402 if it subsequently discontinues 4-log treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same notification and monitoring expectations as for existing sources, with a 30-day compliance monitoring requirement for new sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring effectiveness and reliability of treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A ground water system subject to § 141.403(a) or (b) must monitor the effectiveness and reliability of treatment for that ground water source before or at the first customer as specified in § 141.403(b)(3): chemical disinfection, membrane filtration, or State-approved alternative treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring specifics depend on treatment type and system size (see chemical disinfection subcriteria), and must follow State-specified monitoring and compliance requirements for membrane and alternative treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical disinfection monitoring — systems >3,300 people
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving greater than 3,300 people must continuously monitor the residual disinfectant concentration using analytical methods specified in § 141.74(a)(2) at a State-approved location and must record the lowest residual disinfectant concentration each day that water from the ground water source is served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: System must maintain the State-determined residual disinfectant concentration every day water is served. If continuous monitoring equipment fails, conduct grab sampling every 4 hours until returned to service and resume continuous monitoring within 14 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical disinfection monitoring — systems ≤3,300 people
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving 3,300 or fewer people must monitor the residual disinfectant concentration using methods in § 141.74(a)(2) at a State-approved location and record the residual each day water from the ground water source is served. Take a daily grab sample during peak flow hour or another State-specified time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any daily grab sample falls below the State-determined residual, take follow-up samples every 4 hours until restored. Alternatively, small systems may monitor continuously and meet the larger-system continuous monitoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membrane filtration monitoring and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems using membrane filtration must monitor the membrane filtration process per State-specified monitoring requirements and operate in accordance with State-specified compliance requirements. A membrane filtration system is in compliance with the 4-log virus removal requirement when: (A) the membrane has an absolute MWCO (or alternate parameter) that can reliably achieve at least 4-log removal of viruses; (B) the membrane process is operated per State-specified compliance requirements; and (C) the integrity of the membrane is intact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State specifies monitoring parameters and operational criteria; membrane integrity must be demonstrable under State criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-approved alternative treatment monitoring and operation
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems using a State-approved alternative treatment to provide at least 4-log virus treatment before or at the first customer must: (A) monitor the alternative treatment per State-specified monitoring requirements; and (B) operate the alternative treatment per all compliance requirements the State determines necessary to achieve at least 4-log virus treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative treatments require State approval and State-determined monitoring/operation protocols to ensure equivalent performance to prescribed treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinuing 4-log treatment — State determination required
rubrics_metrics.description: A ground water system may discontinue 4-log treatment of viruses before or at the first customer for a ground water source if the State determines and documents in writing that 4-log treatment is no longer necessary for that ground water source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems that discontinue 4-log treatment become subject to source water monitoring and analytical methods of § 141.402.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring violations require public notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to meet the monitoring requirements of paragraph (b) of this section is a monitoring violation and requires the ground water system to provide public notification under § 141.204.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any failure to meet specified monitoring (chemical, membrane, alternative) triggers public notification obligations under the cited section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment technique violation for uncorrected significant deficiency (120-day rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ground water system with a significant deficiency is in violation of the treatment technique requirement if, within 120 days (or earlier if directed by the State) of receiving written notice from the State of the significant deficiency, the system: (1) does not complete corrective action in accordance with applicable State plan review processes or other State guidance, including State-specified interim actions; or (2) is not in compliance with a State-approved corrective action plan and schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 120-day compliance window (or earlier as directed) applies; failure triggers violation status under § 141.404(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment technique violation for fecal indicator-positive source samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the State invalidates a fecal indicator-positive ground water source sample under § 141.402(d), a ground water system is in violation of the treatment technique requirement if, within 120 days (or earlier if directed by the State) of meeting the conditions of § 141.403(a)(1) or (a)(2), the system: (1) does not complete corrective action per State guidance; or (2) is not in compliance with a State-approved corrective action plan and schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same 120-day corrective-action requirement applies to fecal indicator-positive source findings unless invalidated by the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four-hour correction requirement for loss of 4-log treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: A ground water system subject to § 141.403(b)(3) that fails to maintain at least 4-log treatment of viruses before or at the first customer is in violation of the treatment technique requirement if the failure is not corrected within four hours of determining the system is not maintaining at least 4-log treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate remediation is required; uncorrected failures >4 hours constitute violation under § 141.404(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification for treatment technique violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ground water systems must give public notification under § 141.203 for the treatment technique violations specified in paragraphs (a), (b) and (c) of § 141.404.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific public notification content and timing are governed by § 141.203 and related public notification sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate reporting of State-specified requirement failures
rubrics_metrics.description: A ground water system conducting compliance monitoring under § 141.403(b) must notify the State any time the system fails to meet any State-specified requirements (including minimum residual disinfectant concentration, membrane operating criteria or membrane integrity, and alternative treatment operating criteria) if operation in accordance with the criteria is not restored within four hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be as soon as possible, but in no case later than the end of the next business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting completion of corrective action
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing any corrective action under § 141.403(a), a ground water system must notify the State within 30 days of completion of the corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely notification documents that corrective measures have been implemented as required by State or federal directives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation when source monitoring not conducted per State criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: If a ground water system subject to § 141.402(a) does not conduct source water monitoring under § 141.402(a)(5)(ii), the system must provide documentation to the State within 30 days of the total coliform positive sample that it met the State criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation demonstrates adherence to alternative State criteria in lieu of required source monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — corrective actions (10 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of corrective actions must be kept for a period of not less than ten years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies in addition to general recordkeeping requirements at § 141.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — documentation of public notice (3 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation of notice to the public as required under § 141.403(a)(7) shall be kept for a period of not less than three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records must show compliance with special public notice requirements for significant deficiencies or fecal contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — decisions and invalidation records (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of decisions under § 141.402(a)(5)(ii) and records of invalidation of fecal indicator-positive ground water source samples under § 141.402(d) shall be kept for a period of not less than five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains traceability of State decisions and sample invalidations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — consecutive systems notification (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: For consecutive systems, documentation of notification to the wholesale system(s) of total coliform-positive samples (per relevant sections) shall be kept for a period of not less than five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to documentation of notifications to wholesale systems about total coliform-positive samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — State-specified minimum disinfectant residual (10 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of the State-specified minimum disinfectant residual must be kept for a period of not less than ten years for systems required to perform compliance monitoring under § 141.403(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term retention of the minimum residual requirement documentation for compliance verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — lowest daily residual and failures >4 hours (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of the lowest daily residual disinfectant concentration and records of the date and duration of any failure to maintain the State-prescribed minimum residual disinfectant concentration for a period of more than four hours must be kept for a period of not less than five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports enforcement and trend analysis for disinfectant residual maintenance and outages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping — membrane/alternative treatment compliance records and failures (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records of State-specified compliance requirements for membrane filtration and of parameters specified by the State for State-approved alternative treatment and records of the date and duration of any failure to meet membrane operating, membrane integrity, or alternative treatment operating requirements for more than four hours must be kept for a period of not less than five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents operational compliance and the timeline of significant failures for membrane or alternative treatment systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart T scope — who is subject
rubrics_metrics.description: You are subject to Subpart T if your system: (a) is a public water system; (b) uses surface water or GWUDI as a source; and (c) serves fewer than 10,000 persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart T establishes national primary drinking water regulations for enhanced filtration and disinfection in addition to Subpart H criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven requirements of Subpart T (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are seven requirements of this subpart, and you must comply with all requirements that are applicable to your system: (a) cover finished water reservoirs begun on/after March 15, 2002; (b) updated watershed control for unfiltered systems; (c) develop a disinfection profile for community and non-transient non-community systems unless State determines unnecessary; (d) develop disinfection benchmark and consult State before significant disinfection change; (e) combined filter effluent requirements for filtered systems; (f) individual filter turbidity requirements for conventional or direct filtration; (g) comply with reporting and recordkeeping in §§ 141.570 and 141.571.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must review each listed requirement and determine applicability; the subpart provides detailed sections for each requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finished water reservoir covering requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If your system begins construction of a finished water reservoir on or after March 15, 2002 the reservoir must be covered. Finished water reservoirs for which your system began construction prior to March 15, 2002 are not subject to this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to new construction only; intended to reduce potential post-treatment contamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated watershed control requirements for unfiltered systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Unfiltered Subpart H systems serving fewer than 10,000 persons that do not provide filtration must comply with the filtration avoidance criteria in § 141.71 and additional watershed control requirements in § 141.521 to minimize potential for Cryptosporidium oocyst contamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include identifying watershed characteristics/activities that may adversely affect source water quality and monitoring occurrences of such activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: State determination of watershed control adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: During an onsite inspection under § 141.71(b)(3) the State must determine whether the watershed control program is adequate to limit potential contamination by Cryptosporidium oocysts based on comprehensiveness of watershed review, effectiveness to monitor/control detrimental activities, and extent of land ownership/control within watershed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State evaluation criteria are qualitative and based on program comprehensiveness and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection profile requirement and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A disinfection profile is a graphical representation of your system's level of Giardia lamblia or virus inactivation measured during the course of a year. Subpart H community or non-transient non-community systems serving fewer than 10,000 must develop a disinfection profile unless the State determines it unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State may approve use of a more representative data set for disinfection profiling than the default data set specified in §§ 141.532–141.536.

rubrics_metrics.name: State criteria to deem a disinfection profile unnecessary
rubrics_metrics.description: States may determine a profile is unnecessary only if a system's TTHM and HAA5 levels are below 0.064 mg/L and 0.048 mg/L, respectively; samples used must be collected after Jan 1, 1998, during the warmest month, at the point of maximum residence time in the distribution system. State may approve a more representative TTHM/HAA5 data set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative numeric thresholds for DBPs (TTHM and HAA5) determine exemption from profiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection profile data collection schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A disinfection profile consists of: (a) collecting data for specified parameters once per week on the same calendar day over 12 months; (b) calculating weekly log inactivation per §§ 141.534–141.535; (c) using weekly log inactivations to develop the profile per § 141.536.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems serving 500–9,999 persons must begin data collection no later than July 1, 2003; systems serving <500 persons by Jan 1, 2004 (historical dates from rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameters required to calculate a disinfection profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must monitor: (a) temperature of the disinfected water at each residual disinfectant concentration sampling point during peak hourly flow; (b) pH at each sampling point during peak flow if chlorine is used; (c) disinfectant contact time(s) during peak hourly flow; and (d) residual disinfectant concentration(s) of the water before or at the first customer and prior to each additional point of disinfection during peak hourly flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical methods referenced in § 141.74(a) are to be used; monitoring is weekly on same calendar day over 12 consecutive months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of inactivation ratio and Giardia log inactivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the tables in § 141.74(b)(3)(v) to determine the appropriate CT99.9 value. Calculate the total inactivation ratio (CTcalc/CT99.9) per procedures for single or multiple disinfection points and multiply the value by 3.0 to determine log inactivation of Giardia lamblia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different calculation procedures are provided depending on whether the system uses one or multiple disinfectant application points; successive segment ratios may be summed to compute total inactivation ratio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional viral profiling for certain disinfectants
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system uses chloramines, ozone, or chlorine dioxide for primary disinfection, it must also calculate logs of inactivation for viruses and develop an additional disinfection profile for viruses using methods approved by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-approved methods required for viral profiling when specific disinfectants are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and use of Disinfection Profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Each log inactivation is a data point (52 measurements/year). The system must retain Disinfection Profile data in graphic form (e.g., spreadsheet) available for State sanitary survey review, and use the data to calculate a benchmark if considering changes to disinfection practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention in graphic form facilitates State review and benchmark calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to develop disinfection benchmark before significant changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to develop a Disinfection Profile must develop a Disinfection Benchmark if they decide to make a significant change to disinfection practice and must consult with the State for approval before implementing the significant change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark development and State consultation are prerequisites to implementing significant disinfection practice changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of significant changes to disinfection practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant changes include: (a) changes to the point of disinfection; (b) changes to the disinfectant(s) used in the treatment plant; (c) changes to the disinfection process; or (d) any other modification identified by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must treat these changes as potentially affecting public health and therefore require benchmarking and State consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation package when considering significant disinfection change
rubrics_metrics.description: When considering a significant change, the system must calculate disinfection benchmark(s) and provide the following to the State: (a) description of proposed change; (b) disinfection profile(s) and benchmark(s); (c) analysis of how the change will affect current disinfection levels; and (d) any additional information requested by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive submission enables State evaluation and approval before change implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinfection benchmark calculation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: Determine average Giardia inactivation for each calendar month by dividing sum of inactivations for that month by number of values. Step 2: Determine the lowest monthly average of the twelve values; this value becomes the disinfection benchmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark represents the system's lowest typical monthly disinfection performance and is used to evaluate impacts of proposed disinfection changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viral disinfection benchmark for specific disinfectants
rubrics_metrics.description: If the system uses chloramines, ozone, or chlorine dioxide for primary disinfection, it must calculate the disinfection benchmark from the data collected for viruses in the same manner as the Giardia benchmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate benchmarks may be required for Giardia and for viruses depending on disinfectant used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of combined filter effluent turbidity limits
rubrics_metrics.description: All Subpart H systems serving fewer than 10,000 that are required to filter and utilize filtration other than slow sand or diatomaceous earth must meet the combined filter effluent turbidity requirements of §§ 141.551–141.553. Systems using slow sand or diatomaceous earth must meet § 141.73 limits instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter technology determines which turbidity limits and demonstrations apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two strengthened combined filter effluent turbidity limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must meet two combined filter effluent turbidity limits: (a) a 95th percentile turbidity limit to be met in at least 95% of monthly turbidity measurements; and (b) a maximum turbidity limit that may not be exceeded at any time during the month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement frequency per § 141.74(a) and (c); monthly reporting per § 141.570. Numeric limits depend on filtration technology (e.g., conventional/direct: 95th percentile 0.3 NTU, maximum 1 NTU; alternative filtration: State-determined limits up to specified caps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration requirements for alternative filtration
rubrics_metrics.description: If your system consists of alternative filtration (not slow sand, diatomaceous earth, conventional, or direct), you must conduct a demonstration (e.g., pilot plant studies) to show that filtration, combined with disinfection, consistently achieves: (1) 99% removal of Cryptosporidium oocysts; (2) 99.9% removal and/or inactivation of Giardia lamblia cysts; and (3) 99.99% removal and/or inactivation of viruses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State will use demonstration to establish turbidity limits (not to exceed specified maximums).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lime softening sample acidification provision
rubrics_metrics.description: If your system practices lime softening, you may acidify representative combined filter effluent turbidity samples prior to analysis using a protocol approved by the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State-approved protocol required for sample treatment prior to turbidity analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous individual filter turbidity monitoring requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems using conventional or direct filtration must conduct continuous monitoring of turbidity for each individual filter using an approved method in § 141.74(a); calibrate turbidimeters per manufacturer procedures; record results at least every 15 minutes; complete monthly reporting per § 141.570; and maintain records per § 141.571.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring frequency and calibration ensure real-time detection of filter performance degradations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure on turbidimeter failure
rubrics_metrics.description: If continuous turbidity monitoring equipment fails, systems must conduct grab sampling every four hours in lieu of continuous monitoring until the turbidimeter is back online. The system has 14 days to resume continuous monitoring before a violation is incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term contingency allows continued surveillance; exceeding 14 days triggers violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-or-fewer filters combined monitoring allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If your system only consists of two or fewer filters, you may conduct continuous monitoring of combined filter effluent (CFE) in lieu of individual filter monitoring, meeting the same calibration, recording, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements as for individual filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative monitoring approach for very small filter counts; still subject to same performance and reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up actions for turbidity exceedances — reporting and assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual filter (or CFE for 2-filter systems) exceeds 1.0 NTU in two consecutive 15-minute recordings, report to the State by the 10th of the following month with filter number(s), dates, turbidity values, and cause if known. If this occurs for three months in a row at the same filter, conduct a self-assessment within 14 days including assessment of performance, filter profile development, identification/prioritization of limiting factors, applicability of corrections, and prepare a self-assessment report. If turbidity exceeded 2.0 NTU in two consecutive 15-minute recordings for two months in a row at the same filter, arrange for a Comprehensive Performance Evaluation (CPE) by the State or State-approved third party within 60 days (unless a recent CPE or ongoing CTA project applies); if conducted, CPE must be completed and submitted within 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Escalating responses tied to magnitude and persistence of turbidity exceedances: reporting -> self-assessment -> CPE. Specific timelines and exceptions (recent CPE or CTA involvement) apply.
